summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia, COPD, and a history of recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for hypoxia, respiratory distress, and somnolence following a recent hospital discharge. She presented with tachypnea, increased oxygen needs, and hypercapnia, requiring BIPAP and ICU monitoring. Imaging showed bibasilar atelectasis and right lower lobe consolidation, concerning for aspiration pneumonia. She was treated with cefepime and vancomycin for suspected hospital-acquired pneumonia. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion but required repositioning due to malplacement. Sedating medications including clonazepam were held, and baclofen was reduced to mitigate oversedation and aspiration risk. A swallowing study showed no aspiration, allowing diet advancement. She improved clinically, remained afebrile with negative blood and urine cultures, and was discharged home with services for three additional days of IV antibiotics. Medication adjustments included discontinuation of clonazepam, reduced baclofen, and transition to ranitidine and lower-dose nicotine patch.
